DPI vs PPI: The Difference Explained

DPI stands for dots per inch. PPI stands for pixels per inch. In everyday conversation the terms are often used interchangeably, but they started with different technical meanings.

When to use DPI

DPI is traditionally used for print, scanners, and output devices. A printer rated at 600 DPI means the print head can place 600 ink dots per inch.

When to use PPI

PPI is the more accurate term for screens and digital files. Your monitor has a fixed pixel density. A photo file has pixel dimensions. PPI describes how tightly those pixels are packed.

Does it matter for your calculator results?

For consumer purposes, no. When you use a pixel density calculator, one number describes both display and print use cases. The important factor is using the actual physical size and the actual pixel dimensions.
